# FIDE Swiss Pairing Engine

A Java reference library for the FIDE Swiss pairing systems: it pairs the next round of a Swiss tournament, individual or team, exactly as the FIDE Handbook prescribes, and computes the FIDE tie-breaks. It ships as a library plus a command-line tool that reads and writes FIDE Tournament Report Files (TRF).

> **Not affiliated with or endorsed by FIDE.** "FIDE" names the rules this library implements; it is not a claim of approval.

**Status: pre-alpha.** The Dutch System 2026 pairs rounds and passes every round of a committed corpus generated by its Oracle, bbpPairings v6.0.0; the Dubov, Burstein, Lim and Double-Swiss Systems 2026 and the Olympiad Pairing Rules 2022 pair rounds, checked against a plain enumeration of their text; the C.07 tie-breaks (individual and team) and Standings are in place; the Random Tournament Generator plays whole tournaments and writes them as TRF26; the other systems are not built yet. The specification lives in [`.wayfinder/fide-swiss-engine/map.md`](.wayfinder/fide-swiss-engine/map.md).

The Swiss rules edition and the tie-break edition are chosen explicitly per tournament; the latest is the default.

Statuses follow the definition of done in the Verification strategy: **experimental** (in progress), **Handbook-verified** (with witness review) or **Oracle-verified** (the 50,000-tournament release gate passed).

Every article of the Dutch System 2026 is cited by at least one test, and both of its Handbook worked examples (4.2.2) pass; [`docs/verification/dutch-2026.md`](docs/verification/dutch-2026.md) maps each article to its tests.

### Readings of the Dutch 2026 text

Where the text leaves room, the library follows one documented reading, each verified against bbpPairings v6:

- **4.4.1**: a Limbo "compliant with [C7]" floats the lowest scores actually achievable, not the lowest in the list.
- **[C5]** outranks every quality criterion, so the lowest PAB score the round can reach is fixed before the first bracket, and every bracket keeps it reachable.
- **[C8]** looks one bracket ahead: the most pairs in the following bracket, then the lowest scores of its downfloaters.
- **[C9]** applies when a candidate downfloats exactly one player and nobody below could take the PAB instead.
- **[C18]/[C20]**: a Limbo MDP's score difference is greater than any resident's and grows with its own score.
- Only Numbered Participants (taken into account for this round's pairing or an earlier one) hold a Pairing Number (ADR 0006).

### Readings of the Dutch 2017 text (pre-2026 edition)

Dutch 2017 is its own procedure (A.9: the Penultimate Pairing Bracket and the Collapsed Last Bracket) over the parts Dutch 2026 uses. Where the text leaves room it follows these readings, each what bbpPairings v5.0.1 does:

- **R1 (A.9)** The completion check after a bracket is C.1–C.3 on its downfloaters and every lower player, one PAB-eligible leftover allowed; downfloaters may meet each other there.
- **R2 (A.9, C.4)** The Penultimate Pairing Bracket is paired again with C.4 above C.5 and without C.7; the Collapsed Last Bracket is one heterogeneous bracket (its downfloaters as MDPs, every lower player as a resident).
- **R3 (B.1.c)** M1 is the number of MDPs the optimum pairs, not the most that could be paired.
- **R4 (A.8)** In the Collapsed Last Bracket each player's own score counts for the Pairing Score Difference.
- **R5 (C.7)** The following bracket is paired on C.1–C.3 only and compared on fewest unpaired, then their scores highest first.
- **R6 (C.7, a gap in the text)** When the following bracket is the last, a player it leaves unpaired who may not take the PAB weighs 3 instead of 1.
- **R7 (C.12–C.19)** "The same float" means any float given in this round, with the matching score difference.
- **R8 (A.4.b)** Every round without a played game is a downfloat, absences and forfeit losses included.
- **R9 (C.2)** The PAB and forfeit wins bar the PAB; a requested full-point bye does not.
- **R10 (E.5)** Colour parity uses the Pairing Numbers of Numbered Participants (ADR 0006 holds for 2017 too).
- **R11 (D.3)** Every set of M1 MDPs is tried, by highest different score and then lowest pairing positions; the optimum finder prunes.

### Readings of the Dubov 2026 text

No Oracle exists for Dubov, so the search is checked against a test-scope Literal Enumerator that tries every set of upfloaters, every set of shifters and every transposition in the text's order. Fixed readings:

- **Upfloated** (1.8, [C8]–[C10]) means paired with an opponent who had a higher score when the round was paired, whether or not the game was then played; a bye is never an upfloat.
- **[C9]** adds up the upfloats of the Maximum Upfloaters chosen; read as a count it would only repeat [C8].
- **4.4.1**'s "Article 2.2.4" is 3.2.4, a typo.
- **Shifters** (3.2.4): the first shift takes from the whole smaller subgroup, the equalising shift only from the larger subgroup's own players. In a bracket where nobody has played, the TPN halves take the 4.3.2 order of the colour their subgroup stands for.
- **ARO** is an integer rounded half up (1.7.1), and S1 (3.2.5) and 4.3.2 use the rounded value.
- **3.1.4** "played the highest number of games" counts games played over the board; **5.2.4** compares the colours of games played, from the latest back (GHR 3.4).
- **MaxT** (1.8.2) uses the planned number of rounds.
- **Under acceleration** brackets, the PAB, upfloats (of the round in which the game was paired) and board order read the Pairing Score.

### Readings of the Burstein 2026 text

No Oracle exists for Burstein 2026 (bbpPairings pairs the old text), so the search, one cheapest perfect matching with [C5]–[C8] as digits above the order of 4.3, is checked against a test-scope Literal Enumerator that tries every pairing of a bracket in the order of 4.3 and every pairing of the next bracket for [C7]. Fixed readings:

- **Seeding rounds** (1.6) are paired by the Dutch System 2026 as a whole: its PAB, colours and board order.
- **[C6]** compares the outgoing floaters' scores, sorted descending, as sequences; **[C7]** asks the following bracket (these floaters and the next scoregroup) for its best [C5], then [C6], with [C4] kept; not its [C8].
- **[C8]** counts the pairs whose players want the same colour; a player with no preference (1.5.4) is never denied one.
- **Unplayed rounds** (1.7.2): forfeits and byes are games against oneself for the points registered. The zero-point byes of the exception are requested zero-point byes and the rounds after a Withdrawal.
- **3.1.1** "(forfeit) win" is [C2]: any round scored as a win without playing bars the PAB.
- **Under acceleration** brackets, [C6]/[C7], the PAB and board order read the Pairing Score; the Index reads standings points (1.7.2).
- **Board order** is not in C.04.4.2: the higher Pairing Score, then the lower, then the TPN of the higher-ranked player (1.8).
- **4.3 note** lists `1-3, 2-0, 4-5, 6-0` twice; the order has it once (45 candidates).

### Readings of the Lim 2026 text

Lim is a procedure, not an optimisation: every choice is "the first in this order", and a matching answers only whether the players left can still all be paired and how many pairings a scoregroup can keep. A test-scope Literal Enumerator answers the same questions by trying every pairing. Fixed readings:

- **Floaters** (2.3, 3.1, 3.9, 3.10, 4.4): a scoregroup keeps as many pairings as it can have; the floaters are chosen one at a time by 3.9.2 type (d, c, b, a), then not floated the round before (3.10), then due the colour more players are due (3.2.2), then the lowest numbered (3.2.4/3.3).
- **Numbering**: "highest numbered" is #1 everywhere, "highest pairing number" (3.6, 3.7) included.
- **Median Scoregroup**: rounds played × the points for a win ÷ 2; it always exists, holding only floaters when it has no residents.
- **Compatibility** (2.1): not met, and some colour allocation keeps both inside 5.1.1/5.1.2, counted on played games; in the last round only the meeting counts (Article 6).
- **Floated the round before** (3.10): played the previous round against an opponent with a different score before it.
- **Incoming floaters** are paired first (3.6–3.8), each with the first available player due the other colour, otherwise the first available; *available* means compatible with the rest still pairable.
- **Article 4** is generalised: the first player tries the bottom half in order, then the top half from the bottom up; compatibility and the 5.2 colour exchange are one walk.
- **Edition**: Dubov, Burstein and Lim have only their 2026 text, so a pre-2026 Swiss Rules Edition is rejected (GHR 1.3).
- **Maxi-tournament**: declared by the organiser (`--maxi-tournament`, or `PairingSystems.lim(MaxiTournament.DECLARED)`), never inferred; an exchange for colour (3.8, 5.7) and the colour choice of floater (3.2.3) need ratings within 100 points.
- **Cracking** (2.6): pairings are taken back last made first, from the lower side when more floaters came from above, and the median is paired again.
- **PAB** (1.1): the lowest-ranked eligible player of the lowest scoregroup whose bye leaves the others pairable; round 1 follows 7.1, the lowest rated, unrated counting lowest.
- **Colours** (Article 5): the limits, the due colours, then the history back to the latest difference (5.4), then the higher ranked gets their due colour in the median or above and the lower ranked below it; round parity (5.5/5.6) is read on the player's own played games.
- **Under acceleration** scoregroups, the PAB, 3.10 and board order read the Pairing Score, while the Median Scoregroup keeps its value; an accelerated round 1 therefore has the Accelerated Group above a median of 0 and takes the general procedure, not Article 7.

### Readings of the Double-Swiss 2026 text

C.04.5's 3.3–3.6 are word for word C.04.6's, so Double-Swiss runs the Top-Scoregroup Procedure of the Swiss Team System with its own criteria ([C4]–[C8], no colour criterion) and its own Article 4. No Oracle exists; a test-scope Literal Enumerator tries every set of upfloaters and every pairing of every bracket in the text's orders. No other program implements C.04.5 as written (chesspairing's version has no [C3]–[C7], a colour [C8] and other colour rules; bbpPairings, JaVaFo and Gacrux have none), see [`docs/research/double-swiss-2026-prior-art.md`](docs/research/double-swiss-2026-prior-art.md). Fixed readings:

- **Forfeited match** (Preface): only when a player forfeits both games. It is not a meeting ([C1]) and gives no colour; a match won that way bars the PAB ([C2]), as do a PAB and a full-point bye. When each player forfeits one game, the match is a meeting and counts as played, but gives no colour.
- **Colour** (1.6): the colour scheduled for game 1, when at least one game was actually played. 4.3.1's "yet to play a match" means neither has a colour; 4.3.2 counts Whites, not the colour difference; 4.3.3 compares the played-only histories from their ends (GHR 3.4).
- **Floater** (1.5, [C7], [C8]): met in the previous round (a match not forfeited) an opponent whose score before that round differed. The float criteria lapse only in the planned last round.
- **[C8]** "upfloaters' opponents": the resident paired with an upfloater, as the Swiss Team build reads its [C10], the same words.
- **[C6]** is Swiss Team's Interpretation `upfloater-look-ahead`, default `parity-minimum` (pass or fail), `graded` on request; the following scoregroup is the one right below in the round's standings, the PAB player included.
- **3.1.2**'s "[C.3]" is [C3], and 3.4.1's "a legal pairing for all players" includes [C3]. **3.4.3** counts matches not forfeited, byes excluded.
- **Quality criteria** ("comply as much as possible"): the best value attainable, in priority order, then the first in the text's order.
- **PAB** (1.4): a game won plus a game drawn (1.5) unless `162 P` says otherwise. A requested bye is worth a match: two games won (full-point) or drawn (half-point).
- **Board order** is not in C.04.5: GHR 3.6 on the higher-ranked player of 4.2 (higher score, then smaller TPN).
- **Under acceleration**, Baku's "win" is a match won 2-0: 2 virtual points, then 1. Floats use the Pairing Score by default (`float-score`, as for Swiss Team).
- **TRF** (ADR 0007): match k is TRF rounds 2k−1 and 2k, switched on by `192 FIDE_DOUBLESWISS` or `--double-swiss`; the two columns must agree (same opponent, reversed colours, the same bye in both), and `142` and `250` count TRF rounds. `_BAKU` is provisional, as on every `192` code.

### Readings of the Olympiad Pairing Rules (2022)

D.02 is a team Swiss outside C.04, with a single edition that the system carries, so no edition setting applies. Like Lim it is a procedure, not an optimisation: groups of equal matchpoints from the top down to the Median Group, from the bottom up to it, and the Median Group last; a matching only answers whether the teams left can all be paired, and how many pairings a group can keep (**Kept Pairings**, one perfect matching over the whole round that keeps the most pairings inside the group). A test-scope Literal Enumerator answers the same questions by trying every pairing. No other program implements D.02 (Gacrux/TieBreakServer pairs C.04.6 only, chesspairing mentions the Olympiad only as an example of team events), so there is no Oracle. Fixed readings:

- **Ranking** (3.1, 3.2): the initial pairing number is the library's Pairing Number with 3.1 as the order: `TeamStrength.initialRanking` ranks by the exact average of the four highest ratings (an unrated or missing player counts 0), then the fifth, then the team name. A team file keeps its `310` order, and `Profiles.olympiad` ranks by the team's rating and name. Later rounds rank by matchpoints, then the initial pairing number; game points never count.
- **Bye** (Article 4): the lowest ranked eligible team whose bye leaves the others pairable. 4.2.1 is a PAB; 4.2.2 is a match the opponent forfeited on every board; 4.2.3 is a Late Entry (not on the round-1 list). It is worth 1 matchpoint (4.3); its 2 game points are a drawn match's on the Olympiad's four boards.
- **Met** (6.1): a match with at least one board played. A match lost by default on every board leaves the teams free to meet, and gives no colour (7.7).
- **Median Group** (6.4): of the teams to be paired after the bye, the group of the one at position n/2 + 1 in the 3.2 ranking. It always has residents, is paired downward (9.2), and no floater passes it: 8.2.4/8.3.4's "next group" beyond it is reached through it.
- **Floaters' opponents** (8.2.1, 8.3.1): incoming floaters are paired first, as they arrive (in the Median Group the downfloaters, highest ranked first, then the upfloaters, lowest ranked first). A downfloater takes the highest ranked team of the group, an upfloater the lowest ranked, residents before other floaters; "which it has not already played" means an opponent with which the group still reaches its Kept Pairings. A floater without one moves on.
- **A group's floaters** (8.2.2–8.2.3, 8.3.2–8.3.3, 8.4, 9.4, 9.5): the group floats exactly the teams it cannot keep; each is the first, in the text's order, whose move still reaches Kept Pairings, a team with an opponent in the adjacent group first. Because every step is asked of the whole round, 8.4 never has to undo a floater.
- **9.3**: "against N − 1, N − 2 and so on" means N, N − 1, … 2, as the six-team example shows (its row 4 misprints 3 x 5 for 3 x 6); "the subgroup is unsolvable" means the rest of the group cannot all be paired. Below the median the same order runs on the mirrored ranking (9.2).
- **7.3 and 7.4**: the limits count played matches only and are part of compatibility; 7.4 disregards them for a group whenever keeping them would make it keep fewer pairings (float more teams), not only when it would otherwise need no floater at all.
- **Colours of board 1** (7.5–7.7), for the higher ranked team: a colour that breaks 7.3 for either team is not given when the other is possible; then equalisation (the team with the larger colour difference gets Black; 7.6's "white the same number of times" is read as the same colour difference); then alternation from the latest round in which the two had different colours; then the higher ranked team alternates from its last colour (the lower ranked one's, if only it has one); with no colours, 7.2: the colour drawn by lot (`152`) when the higher ranked team's pairing number is odd, the other when it is even.
- **Publication order** (11.1): the boards are numbered by the higher ranked team's matchpoints, the sum of both, then the higher ranked team's rating (its 3.1.1 average: the `310` strength), each highest first, then its pairing number. 11.2 and 11.3 are the arbiter's.
- **Not in the library**: unfinished games (5.1, 5.2; record a draw and correct it later, the published pairing stands), and articles 2, 10, 11.2 and 11.3 (host teams, who is paired, dropping a team short of players), which reach it as Late Entries, Withdrawals and absences. D.02 has no acceleration: a Baku or explicit acceleration, and `FIDE_OLYMPIAD_BAKU`, are refused. The check reports 7.3 only when board 1's colours break a limit the other colours would keep.

### Readings of the C.07 text

The Tie-break Edition alone fixes every value; each reading below stands on the text (Tie-break interpretation rulings):

- Art. 16 (Adjusted Score, Dummy Opponent, the 16.5 cut exception) governs BH, FB, SB and their Cut/Median modifiers, and AOB through BH/FB. PS, ARO and KS count their own values: PS/C1 drops the round-1 score even after a bye.
- 16.4.2's "number of rounds" is the rounds the Standings count, so the cap binds mid-tournament too.
- `/P`: a forfeit is a game against the scheduled opponent at its Adjusted Score, not a Voluntary Unplayed Round. For DE it includes forfeits (6.1.1).
- FB draws every paired game of the final round, forfeits included; byes keep their points.
- TPR and PTP score games 1 / ½ / 0; p is rounded half up to two decimals; TPR adds dp to the rounded ARO; PTP uses the full 8.1.2 scale (100% gives the highest opponent + 736), and a zero score gives the lowest opponent − 800.
- DE 6.3: a participant is placed first when its lowest possible score beats every other's highest, repeated meetings averaged; at the first place that cannot be decided, art. 6 is reapplied to those still tied.
- REP subtracts every round after a withdrawal (a zero-point bye, 16.1.1) and a double forfeit (a forfeit loss for both).
- A double forfeit is a forfeit loss for both participants; a "less than one move" game (TRF `W`/`D`/`L`) is a game played.
- Rating tie-breaks are dropped (they separate nobody) when any participant is unrated (art. 10).
- Virtual points never enter a tie-break.
- Ties that survive the whole list share a rank: the library never draws lots.

Team tie-breaks (art. 11–13), where the text leaves room:

- A team's Score is its primary score, match points or game points (TRF `192`); `:MP` or `:GP` on WIN, WON, PS, BH, AOB, FB and KS computes that tie-break in the named score (13 preamble), the primary score being the default. A round's other-score points come from the match itself: a bye is worth a drawn match's points in the other score too (C.04.6 1.4).
- WIN and WON count won matches and are always in match points (the Technical Commission's table lists only `:MP`); `:GP` is refused. Dummy caps of 16.4.2 use a draw's points in the score read, times the rounds.
- ESB: a term is (opponent's total in one score) × (points scored against it in the other); the Dummy Opponent's total is the team's own capped total in the opponent's score; Cut-1 ranks the terms by the opponent's total, then the product (14.1.2); art. 16.5 applies as for SB. A bare `ESB` is refused: name one of the four.
- EDE: Direct Encounter on the primary score; if that separates nobody, on the secondary score; every new subset restarts from the primary score (13.3.3). The knock-out tie-breaks of EDEBT/EDEBB/EDET/EDEB apply, in the order of the name, only to exactly two teams tied in both match and game points (13.3.2). For BC, a lower sum ranks higher, so among two tied teams EDEBT/EDEBB rank the lower Board Count first; Gacrux's EDEBT ranked the higher one first on the hand-worked round robin, which contradicts 12.1.
- BC, TBR, BBE (12): forfeited games are standard results and a PAB is a win's points on every board, whatever the game points actually credited. BC is not usable (no value) among teams with different game points (12.1). TBR compares board 1's game points, then board 2's (each board alone, not cumulative); BBE compares the game points of boards 1..n-1, then 1..n-2, and so on down to board 1 (12.2, 12.3).
- SSSC: secondary score + Buchholz on the primary score (Fore Buchholz with `/F`) / normalising factor; the factor is (rounds of the tournament × the win value of the primary score) / (the win value of the other score in one match), truncated, at least 1, or `/Kx`. Match points are 2 per win, so with 4 boards and 9 rounds the factor is 18 / 4 = 4 in match points and 36 / 2 = 18 in game points.
- The board of a game is its position in the match (line-up order), the same for both teams.

The `individualSwiss` profile uses `BH/C1, BH, SB, DE` under C.07 2026-03. That list is our choice; C.07 2.1 leaves it to the organiser.

## Library

```java
var tournament = Tournament.of(participants, NumberOfRounds.of(9));   // Dutch 2026, 1 / ½ / 0
var historic = Tournament.of(
        Profiles.individualSwiss(NumberOfRounds.of(9)).with(SwissRulesEdition.PRE_2026), participants); // Dutch 2017
var pairing = tournament.pairNextRound();
tournament = tournament.withRound(pairing.completedWith(outcomes));    // outcomes by board
tournament = tournament.requestBye(id, RoundNumber.of(4), RequestedBye.half());
tournament = tournament.withdraw(id, RoundNumber.of(6));
tournament = tournament.enterLate(participant, RoundNumber.of(2));      // or MissedRounds.halfPointByes()
tournament = tournament.withCorrectedOutcome(round, id, outcome);      // also colours and ratings (GHR 4.3)
var check = tournament.check(ProposedPairing.of(boards, bye));         // violations, differences
var why = pairing.about(id);                                           // bracket, floats, opponent, colour rule
tournament.pairNextRound(progress);                                    // PairingProgress; interrupt to cancel
var standings = tournament.standings();                                // or standingsAfter(round)
standings.compare(a, b).decidedBy();                                   // score, a tie-break, or a shared rank
```

The `generator` module plays whole tournaments through this API, so it only produces valid input:

```java
var settings = GeneratorSettings.of(Profiles.individualSwiss(NumberOfRounds.of(9)))   // rounds are drawn
        .withPlayers(Range.of(20, 60))
        .withLateEntryPercentage(Range.of(0, 5))
        .withRandomAcceleration()                                     // Baku for 20% of the tournaments
        .withRandomTieBreaks();                                       // 3-5 tie-breaks drawn per tournament
var generated = TournamentGenerator.of(settings).generate(CorpusSeed.of(42).tournament(7));
// Completed(seed, tournament, parameters) or Skipped(seed, round, reason, parameters)
```

- Each tournament draws its own parameters. The defaults follow bbpPairings v6's generator: 15–215 players, 5–15 rounds (at most players − 1), the highest rating 2400–2800 and the lowest 1400–2300 with ratings uniform between them, 0–10% unrated (with a hidden strength), a forfeit in 1 of 6–30 games with each side absent independently (so 0F-0F occurs), half- and zero-point byes in 1 of 15–3225 player-rounds (never in the last round, at most two per participant), no full-point byes, 0–5% withdrawals after a random round and 0–5% late entries in round 2 to ⌈rounds/2⌉. The initial colour is drawn and always written.
- Results follow Milvang's model (C.02.03 §7.2.4) with the white advantage; a `DrawPercentage` switches to a flat draw share. `withRandomScoring()` scores 10% of the tournaments 3/1/0 or 2/1/0 (never a Double-Swiss one); Baku is only applied where the scoring allows it (C.04.7 1.1).
- A team system generates team tournaments: `GeneratorSettings.ofTeams(Profiles.teamSwiss(rounds))` or `ofTeams(Profiles.olympiad(rounds))` (8–40 teams, 5–11 rounds at most teams − 2, 2–6 boards, four for the Olympiad, distinct strengths), each match a `MatchOutcome` over the boards with the boards' strengths falling from board 1, forfeits per board and whole-team no-shows; `withRandomTeamFormat()` draws the Swiss Team's match points, primary score, secondary score and colour preference type, and `withRandomTieBreaks()` draws from the team tie-breaks of C.07 art. 12–13. The writer writes them as team files (`310`, `352`, `362`, a block per board on each member's line) that read back to the same matches.
- A Double-Swiss match plays two games with the colours reversed, each from the result model; a player absent for the match forfeits both games, and a player present may still forfeit one, at the same rate.
- `TournamentModel.applyTo(settings, tournament)` replays a model tournament's field and settings with the forfeit, bye and withdrawal rates observed in it. `RtgConfiguration.applyTo(settings, text)` reads JaVaFo/bbp `Key=Value` files: `PlayersNumber`, `RoundsNumber`, `DrawPercentage`, `ForfeitRate`, `RetiredRate`, `HalfPointByeRate`, `HighestRating`, `LowestRating`, `PointsForWin`, `PointsForDraw`, `PointsForLoss`; a missing key keeps its random default.
- The PRNG is the JDK's `L64X128MixRandom`. Tournament *k* of a corpus has the seed SplitMix64(corpus seed, *k*), and every draw uses a substream keyed by seed, round and purpose, or for a result by seed, round, players and board, so one tournament is reproducible alone and a pairing change only changes what depends on it. Reproduction holds per generator version.
- When a round has no legal pairing the tournament is `Skipped`, never bent; a corpus skips too many above 0.1%.

Profiles: `Profiles.individualSwiss(rounds)` (the baseline), `Profiles.acceleratedOpen(rounds)` (with Baku) `Profiles.doubleSwiss(rounds)` (two-game matches, the PAB worth 1½; outcomes are `MatchOutcome.ofGames(List.of(game1, game2))`, each game seen from game 1's White), `Profiles.teamSwiss(rounds)` and `Profiles.olympiad(rounds)` (the Olympiad Pairing Rules over four boards at 2/1/0, the bye worth 1 matchpoint; rank the teams by 3.1 with `with(TeamStrength.initialRanking(teams, strengths))`; outcomes are `MatchOutcome.ofGames(boards)`, each board seen from board 1's White team). Any setting can be overridden with `with(...)`, for example `with(Acceleration.explicit(virtualPoints))` or `with(InitialColour.black())`.

- Acceleration: the Pairing Score (Score plus the round's Virtual Points) is the score wherever the text says score, floats and board order included; standings never see it. Baku's Accelerated Group is the top 2·⌈N/4⌉ of the round-1 list, and a Late Entry ranked above its last participant joins it (C.04.7 1.3).
- A rating correction renumbers until four rounds are recorded, and no longer after that (GHR 2.3).


Each `Standing` holds its rank, Score and tie-break values in list order, and `decidedBy()` against the participant directly above when both have the same Score. Each value carries its per-round contributions (the opponent or the Dummy Opponent, the value used, what cut or adjusted it, with the article).

The pairing carries its boards in GHR 3.6 order, the PAB, everyone left out with the reason, the Pairing Numbers it used and a trace of the brackets and colour rules.

## Command line

The full user manual, for arbiters and developers, is in [`docs/manual.md`](docs/manual.md).

```sh
fide-swiss pair <in.trf> [-o <reply>] [-l [<trace>]]      # canonical
fide-swiss [--dutch|--dubov|--burstein|--lim|--double-swiss|--swiss-team|--olympiad] <in.trf> -p [<reply>] [-l [<trace>]] # JaVaFo / bbpPairings form
fide-swiss check <in.trf> [--round <r>]                   # also <in.trf> -c [<r>] and -check <in.trf>
fide-swiss standings <in.trf> [--after <r>] [--why <id> <id>]
fide-swiss generate -o <out%d.trf> [--seed <n>] [--count <k>] [--profile <name>] [--config <cfg>] [--model <in.trf>] [flags]
fide-swiss -g [<cfg>|<seed>] -o <out.trf> [-s <seed>] [--dubov|--burstein|--lim|--double-swiss]   # JaVaFo / bbpPairings form
fide-swiss version                                        # also -r
```

- The Pairing Reply is JaVaFo's: the number of lines, then one `white black` line per board using the file's own ids, and the PAB as `id 0` last.
- `check` re-pairs every recorded round from the rounds before it and prints each ILLEGAL round (with the articles broken) or DIFFERENT round (the file's and the system's pairing). Without `--round` it also checks the standings after the last round: the file's Points must equal the computed scores, and a stated rank must fall inside the computed shared-rank range (under the file's `202`/`212`, or within the participant's score group when the file names no list).
- `standings` prints rank, id, name, score, one column per tie-break and a `decided by` column; `--why` prints the Deciding Tie-break of two participants with every contribution of both values. The list comes from `212` (without its `PTS`) or `202`, else the profile's.
- `pair --explain <id>` writes that participant's explanation to stderr (or into the `-l` trace); `--quiet` suppresses the progress line, which otherwise appears on a terminal's stderr after 500 ms. Ctrl-C exits with 130 without writing a reply.
- Flags override the file's records: `--system dutch|dubov|burstein|lim|double-swiss|swiss-team|olympiad` (or `--dutch`, `--dubov`, `--burstein`, `--lim`, `--double-swiss`, `--swiss-team`, `--olympiad`; a file with `310` records is a team file and only takes `--swiss-team` or `--olympiad`; `double-swiss` reads two TRF rounds per match, ADR 0007), `--interpretation <name>=<value>` (a Swiss Team or Double-Swiss reading, repeatable; Double-Swiss takes the first and the last: `upfloater-look-ahead=parity-minimum|graded`, `last-round-zero-cd-type-b=strong|none`, `float-score=pairing|real`), `--maxi-tournament` (Lim only; no TRF record exists), `--edition 2026|pre-2026` (the Swiss Rules Edition, over `192`), `--rounds <n>` (over `142`/`XXR`), `--initial-colour white|black` (over `152`/`XXC`), `--tiebreaks "<list>"` (over `202`/`212`), `--tiebreak-edition 2026-03|2024-08`.
- Record `192` selects the system: `FIDE_DUTCH`, `FIDE_DUTCH_2026` (alias `FIDE_DUTCH_2025`), `FIDE_DUTCH_2017` (the pre-2026 edition), `FIDE_DUBOV`, `FIDE_DUBOV_2026`, `FIDE_BURSTEIN`, `FIDE_BURSTEIN_2026`, the provisional `FIDE_LIM` (alias `FIDE_LIM_2026`; TRF26 has no Lim code), `FIDE_DOUBLESWISS` (alias `FIDE_DOUBLESWISS_2026`, which also switches on two TRF rounds per match), each optionally with `_BAKU`, the Swiss Team codes `FIDE_TEAM_…`, and the provisional `FIDE_OLYMPIAD` for a team file paired by the Olympiad Pairing Rules (TRF26 has no Olympiad code; `FIDE_OLYMPIAD_BAKU` is refused, D.02 has no acceleration). A bare code means the 2026 rules, never the tournament date; any other code is rejected (exit 3) until its system is built. bbpPairings writes the code in `092`, which is read the same way when there is no `192`.
- `generate` writes one TRF26 file per tournament (`%d` is its index) named `RTG <version> seed <n>` in `012`, and with `--count` above 1 a `<pattern>.manifest.tsv` with each seed's status and effective parameters. Without `--seed` a fresh corpus seed is printed on stderr. Precedence: the profile (`--profile individual-swiss|accelerated-open|double-swiss`), then `--config` or `--model`, then the flags. A number fixes a parameter and `A..B` draws it per tournament: `--players`, `--rounds`, `--highest-rating`, `--lowest-rating`, `--unrated <%>`, `--forfeit-rate`, `--hpb-rate`, `--zpb-rate`, `--fpb-rate` (1 in N; 0 never), `--withdrawals <%>`, `--late-entries <%>`, `--draw-percentage <P>`. Tournament flags: `--system dutch|dubov|burstein|lim|double-swiss` (or `--dutch`, `--dubov`, `--burstein`, `--lim`, `--double-swiss`, also after `-g`), `--maxi-tournament` (Lim), `--edition 2026|pre-2026`, `--tiebreak-edition 2026-03|2024-08`, `--acceleration none|baku|random`, `--tiebreaks "<list>"|random`, `--random-scoring`.
- The reader takes TRF26 and TRF16 with CR, LF or CRLF line endings, UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1. A last round column holding only `0000 - H/F/Z` marks means those participants are absent from the round to be paired.

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | no legal pairing |
| 2 | unexpected internal error |
| 3 | invalid request or input |
| 4 | size limit (reserved for bbp compatibility, never emitted) |
| 5 | file access error |
| 6 | the check found inconsistencies |
| 7 | `generate` skipped more than 0.1% of its seeds |

## Modules

| Artifact | Contents |
|---|---|
| `fide-swiss-pairing-engine-core` | Domain model, handling rules, every pairing system, acceleration, tie-breaks. No runtime dependencies. |
| `fide-swiss-pairing-engine-trf` | TRF reader and writer. |
| `fide-swiss-pairing-engine-generator` | Random Tournament Generator: the library playing whole tournaments with a result model. Depends only on `core`. |
| `fide-swiss-pairing-engine-cli` | Command-line pairing, checking and tournament generation. |

Group id: `io.github.markdechamps`, one version for every module. Not yet published to Maven Central; releases will go there through the Central Portal (`release.yml`, see `CHANGELOG.md`).

The command line ships as a portable `fide-swiss-X.Y.Z.zip` (`bin/fide-swiss`, `lib/` with the modular jars; needs Java 25 on the path) and, per release, as jlink images for linux-x64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64 and windows-x64 that need no Java. On macOS, remove the quarantine attribute and run the image from a terminal.

## Building

Requires Java 25 (`sdk env` picks up the version pinned in `.sdkmanrc`).

```sh
./mvnw verify                 # tests, formatting check, coverage report
./mvnw spotless:apply         # format the code
git config core.hooksPath .githooks   # run the tests before every commit
```
